prompt:
Use the attached image as the reference: the same woman — the personification of Vanadium (V) — seen off duty in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye colour, hair colour, skin tone and body exactly; change only her clothes, pose and place. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

Face: exactly the attached image's face — the same short midface and face length-to-width ratio; the camera angle, pose, bangs or a headpiece never make her face look longer or her jaw heavier.

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Hair: her hair tied up in a loose bun or ponytail — same colour and length as the attached image, a few strands loose.
Light direction: dappled light — patches of light with leaf or blind shadow across her.
Outfit: a 1920s bias-cut satin lounge gown — in warm earth tones such as camel, olive, rust, chocolate or burgundy; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance; right now — a sudden rain shower or a splash of water has just soaked her clothes — the damp fabric clings to her body line and darkens in patches, a few wet strands of hair stick to her neck and cheek; the fabric stays opaque, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.

Lens / perspective: 50mm-equivalent natural perspective with balanced proportions and modest depth compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand is in PROP.
PROP: with both hands she lifts a small storage box onto the shelf above her — her own right hand under the right side of the box, her own left hand under the left side.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — vanadium: a hard steel-grey metal named in 1830 for Vanadis, the Norse goddess of beauty, because its compounds come in so many fine colours; dissolved, it changes colour with each charge, violet, green, blue and yellow; first found in 1801 in a brown lead ore in Mexico and called erythronium for salts that turn red when heated, then given up as mere chromium; a pinch of it makes steel tough, and traces of it hid in the watered patterns of old Damascus blades; sea squirts gather it in their blood; tanks of its four-coloured solutions store power in great flow batteries — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.
